📰 General

Apple Rolls Out New Firmware Updates for AirPods Pro and Beats Studio Buds •

Apple has released new firmware updates for its AirPods Pro 3 and AirPods Pro 2 headphones. The updates, designated version 8B41, represent an upgrade from the previous 8B40 version for the AirPods Pro 3 and 8B39 for the AirPods Pro 2. Details regarding the specific changes introduced by the firmware remain undisclosed at this time. The updates are available for download through the standard Apple firmware update process. Users can check for and install the updates within the Find My app.

🌍 World

Norwegian Royal Family Shaken: Crown Prince’s Son Convicted of Serious Crimes •

Marius Borg Høiby, the 29-year-old son of Norway’s Crown Princess Mette-Marit, was found guilty by a Norwegian court of rape and domestic violence. The court sentenced him to a four-year prison term following the conviction. The charges relate to allegations of sexual assault involving a minor. Legal proceedings are ongoing, and the case has significant implications for the Norwegian royal family.

🦅 US

Trump’s White House Ballroom Project Will Be Funded by Taxpayer Dollars •

Newly released documents confirm that Donald Trump’s planned ballroom addition to the White House will be funded entirely by taxpayer money. The president previously asserted that the project would not cost the government any funds. The documents, obtained by The Washington Post, detail the significant expense associated with the construction. The project’s total cost is estimated to be over $30 million, encompassing design, construction, and ongoing maintenance.

💰 Business

DOJ Sides With Musk’s xAI in National Security Lawsuit Against NAACP •

The Department of Justice and the state of Mississippi have filed a motion to intervene in a lawsuit brought by the NAACP against xAI, Musk’s artificial intelligence company. The legal challenge alleges that xAI’s business operations constitute a matter of national security. The NAACP initially argued that xAI’s AI models could be used to discriminate against Black people. This intervention marks a significant escalation in the legal battle surrounding xAI’s development and potential impact.

💻 Technology

Google Earth Launches Browser-Based Flight Simulator Mode for Global Access •

Google Earth has introduced a new flight simulator mode accessible directly through a web browser. Users can now experience virtual flight globally without needing to download or install any software. The feature utilizes Google Earth’s existing 3D imagery and allows for interactive flight control. This browser-based mode offers a simplified and readily available alternative to more complex flight simulation programs. It’s currently available to anyone with a web browser.

🎭 Entertainment

NBCUniversal Consolidates UCP & Universal International Studios Under New Leadership •

NBCUniversal is streamlining its television operations with the merger of UCP and Universal International Studios under the leadership of Beatrice Springborn. Pearlena Igbokwe, previously Chairman of Television Studios, will oversee the integration of the two studios, marking a shift from a four-division structure to three. This consolidation is expected to improve efficiency and streamline content development across the NBCUniversal portfolio. The move follows long-rumored discussions and is anticipated to impact staffing levels within the combined organization.

🏅 Sports

Tartan Army’s Boston Blitz: Scottish Fans Consume Massive Quantities of Beer •

Following a 1-0 victory against Haiti, a large contingent of Scottish soccer supporters, known as the “Tartan Army,” descended upon Boston. These fans frequented numerous restaurants and pubs throughout the city, celebrating their win. Notably, they attended a Boston Red Sox game at Fenway Park, further immersing themselves in the city’s atmosphere. Authorities reported a significant increase in beer sales during the period of the Tartan Army’s visit.

🔬 Science

NASA Issues Amendment 59, Raising Concerns Over Political Influence in Science •

NASA recently released Amendment 59 to the ROSES-25 Summary of Solicitation, prompting criticism regarding potential political bias within the agency’s scientific processes. The amendment includes language describing a “lack of transparency” and “accountability,” raising concerns about the influence of political considerations on scientific priorities. Critics argue this phrasing demonstrates a departure from NASA’s historical commitment to objective scientific evaluation. The document outlines updates to the solicitation, focusing on criteria for research proposals. This development has ignited debate about the role of political influence in scientific funding decisions at the agency.

🩺 Health

Measles Case Detected at SFO, Raising Concerns Ahead of World Cup •

A confirmed case of measles has been identified at San Francisco International Airport, prompting a public health alert. The individual, a traveler, was detected days before the FIFA World Cup begins, raising concerns about potential exposure. Santa Clara County Public Health officials are investigating the source of the virus and monitoring for further cases. They are advising travelers to be aware of symptoms and to consult a healthcare provider if necessary. The airport is working with public health officials to implement preventative measures.
